title: Proof-run cases for whole C:\ (finished and stopped), a real OneDrive and a real share, with counts-only records under docs/proof-runs
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

The verdict: the proposal gave Get-W001Verdict a refusedAnotherCode parameter. This design adds that count to the leak argument and gives it its own Check, as leaks already have, so the signature does not change. Either works.

The plant rows: the proposal removed S83-S86 and P36 without replacement. This design re-plants the same five texts at docs/proof-runs under new ids. A reviewer reading the constraint's 'only the plant rows that point at .taad/slices are removed' more strictly may disagree.
Copying coverage: by a named field list (the proposal) or by a walk that drops strings (this design).
Compare-StoppedRows keeps six classes. Merging codeChanged into notInFinished would be simpler, at the cost of the console naming which happened.
The -Force guard against overwriting a stopped part is a small convenience that could be dropped, since git shows the change anyway.

The maintainer's own runs: W-001 -Root C:\ -Stopped (finished and stopped whole-C:\ record, criteria C1b, C2, C3, C5), W-002 -Root on their OneDrive (C8), and W-003 -Root on a real share over home and Tailscale (C9). They are the person's (kernel pool held until a restart, their own account, physical cuts). No record exists under docs/proof-runs yet and none should be committed from this build.

W-002 on its CfProvider rig and W-003 on the loopback stall rig were built and are covered in their pure parts, but were not run here: they register a cldflt sync root and map an SMB loopback share, which this project gates to a person or validate. The real mode of W-003 (the prompts, the typed 'cut', the marker file) has never been run.
A hook change for the 60 s marker deadline was not built, as O-003 decided; a missed deadline ends W-003 real mode inconclusive with a record.

Validate should run tests/window/SL-003-W002OnTheCloudRig.Tests.ps1 and SL-003-W003OnTheStallRig.Tests.ps1 (or the planted E003-4 and E003-5) with a person's allowance, since they register a sync root and map a loopback share.

If the engine plants E003-1, its `-not (Test-Path .taad\slices)` line must be replaced by Q-010's two checks: `git grep -n -i taad -- tests/window/WindowCases.ps1` prints nothing, and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .taad` shows nothing new. Any planted E003 script must remove the docs/proof-runs files it creates.

After the maintainer's C:\ run, read the record for Q-001 (unseen against the measured $MFT, whose bytes are in measured[0]) and Q-002 (panelTop, textsHeight, textsOffset). Lesson #872 stands: the C:\ shape is not validated until then.
If W-003 real mode ends inconclusive because of the hook's 60 s marker deadline, the record is the evidence for an additive FSA_HOOK_MARKER_DEADLINE_S (default 60) in a later slice.
Seam.Probe's second open duplicates Seam.Times; Probe could call Times. Left as is to keep the oracle's existing behaviour untouched.

deviation: Coverage's 'folders' array is written as two counts (unreadable, notScanned), not as the walk's copy of it. Its only data is each folder's kind, a word, so a walk that drops strings would leave hundreds of empty entries for a whole C:\. 'measured' keeps only bytes under the same walk. The design says the walk copies the figures; the rest is that walk.

deviation: -Case All is filtered inline in the existing `$cases = if ($Case -eq 'All') { ... | Where-Object { $_ -notin $ProofCases } }` statement, not through a new function. WindowCasesHelperTests.AllLeavesOutTheTimingCases reads that statement, and a first attempt with a Get-CaseList function broke it. The new test evaluates the script's own statement.

deviation: I added three finish-line scripts the design does not list (tests/window/SL-003-W001OnASubstDrive.Tests.ps1, SL-003-W002OnTheCloudRig.Tests.ps1, SL-003-W003OnTheStallRig.Tests.ps1), so that the case obligations have a command that feeds the real shape. The design's E003-1 to E003-5 scripts are engine-planted and not in the tree. If the engine plants them, the old E003-1 line `-not (Test-Path .taad\slices)` still cannot pass on uat (Q-010); it is the engine's to rewrite.

deviation: I added small pure helpers beyond the design's list so each rule can be tested: Get-LeakCount, Get-WholeDriveReportGaps, Save-ProofRecord, Test-KeptStoppedPart, New-StoppedPart, New-HydrationRecord, New-ShareRecord, Get-CutFolderRows, Get-ShareVerdict, Get-RoundedOrNull. Get-W001Verdict's signature is unchanged. The refused-another-code count goes through Get-LeakCount.

deviation: The guard runner SL-107-RecordPathRule.Tests.ps1 reads plain (unquoted) YAML scalars as well as single-quoted ones, because the engine-appended entry's patterns are unquoted. I did not change the appended entry.
deviation: The reason-belongs-to-code check is required on a local letter only and recorded elsewhere, as the design says. The refused-another-code check applies to every root.

deviation: No product code and no hook code was changed. No outside-defect workaround is involved, so no new setting or notice was added.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-002: unsettled design fork: Does the hook's stop mode, triggered by FSA_HOOK_AT_FOLDERS, run together with FSA_HOOK_ROWS=1 and leave a full rows dump and closing line on the stopped ending? Its context: For yes, from the code: StartupHook.cs:365 allows FSA_HOOK_ROWS for stop, 496-502 routes stop with a progress trigger to DriveAtProgress, and RowsMode subscribes to EndingShown on its own. Against: no case has ever run the pair. N-005 uses ARMED with ROWS; SL-001 case H uses AT_FOLDERS without ROWS. E003-3 settles it at build. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: MEASURE in the risk spike before anything is built. Do not let E003-3 settle it at build. Setup (spike, non-elevated, interactive desktop, TAAD3_HOME, TEMP and TMP set to a fresh scratch folder): 1. Publish the app and build FsaWindowHook from a clone of the slice's HEAD. The hook is unchanged in the design, so HEAD's hook is the one under test. 2. In scratch %TEMP%, make a TAAD-owned tree in this shape: two folders created first, each with a Deny ListDirectory ACE for the current user, then 30,000 empty folders (for example 300 x 100). This is E003-3's shape and is above lesson #877's 24,000-folder floor. 3. SUBST a free letter over the tree. Read paged and nonpaged kernel pool before the runs. Runs (use the same hooked launch the harness makes, Invoke-HookedRun or the identical DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS launch, with `"<L>:\" --report`, and keep every hook log): - R0, finished: mode rows, FSA_HOOK_ROWS=1. Read F = core.folders and the rows. - R1 to R3, stopped: mode stop, FSA_HOOK_AT_FOLDERS=floor(F/2), FSA_HOOK_ROWS=1, wait up to 600 s. Record for each stopped run: - app exit code, core.status and outcome; - the full 'acted mode=stop ...' line, with its atfolders, folders and sized fields and its ms; - whether there is a 'rows read count=n ... ms=' line; - whether there is a closing 'rows' line with count, elevated and stopUtc; - the number of row lines; - every 'refused' line (in particular a refusal of FSA_HOOK_ROWS for this mode, or 'the scan ended before the trigger'); - rows against the header's N against core.unreadable; - whether every stopped row's path is in R0's rows with the same kind and code; - whether any row has code 995. Afterwards: remove the SUBST and the deny ACEs, delete the tree, and read kernel pool again. How the result decides the fork: - YES, the design stands as written (no hook change, E003-3 and -Stopped keep their shape): on all three stopped runs, status is Cancelled; the acted line shows sized '-'; both the 'rows read' line and the closing rows line are present; and the row lines = closing count = header N = core.unreadable. - NO, the hook needs a change and the design is written again for it: the hook refuses FSA_HOOK_ROWS together with the progress trigger; or the stop acts but on any run the 'rows read' line, the closing line or the row dump is missing or disagrees with the report. - Not decided yet, so enlarge the tree to 60,000 folders and repeat: the trigger never acts during the listing (Completed, 'ended before the trigger', or sized not '-') on all three runs. Bring back as well, as data for the rewrite but not as part of the decision: the exact acted-line text, which confirms m3's ' folders=(\d+) ' and ' sized=(\S+) ' parse; and whether 'acted ... ms=' and 'rows read ... ms=' share one clock, which W-003's Read-StopTiming relies on. Nothing measured so far answers this. The code reading for yes (StartupHook.cs:365, 376-377, 496-502) has never been run: N-005 pairs ARMED with ROWS, and SL-001 case H pairs AT_FOLDERS without ROWS. The losing answer forces a hook change, which the design rules out and lesson #472 says a builder must not patch in. Leaving it to E003-3 at build is exactly the 'settled by writing code' this stage exists to prevent. Reality can settle it cheaply and safely: a TAAD-made %TEMP% tree of about 30,000 empty folders and four hooked launches, the same kind the w001-oracle spike already made on this PC, with no whole-drive scan and no person's step. The same runs also give O-001 ('the second run really is partial') its first observation, and fix the acted-line parse that m3 depends on. Both laps are still available. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
